FerryDock / separate live SDK experiment

Five original variants.
Plus .NET MAUI.

The same minimal container list, now backed by container-zig, the official Moby Go client, Bollard, a separate Zig integration of the C libdocker SDK, and Slint with a CPU renderer and Bollard. Each app reads Docker Engine directly at startup and wires manual Refresh to the same loading function.

All five loaded the same live inventory. Container IDs are compared using SHA-256 of sorted full IDs joined by a newline, with no trailing newline. The reference digest is 9b3587c9a02aefc52a6ad2b5c04fb1ba6e3615c0673b13bf87ce0bc1db2ff931. The UI, fields, and profiles are retained from the original comparison. The Zig SDK is experimental; see the dependency-maturity assessment below. The original four-integration JSON/CLI report remains separate.

SDK selection: the Zig dependency is experimental

This is not a maturity-equivalent SDK comparison. The Zig prototype uses a young, unofficial client with very limited public adoption evidence. Its successful container-list request and low resource usage do not establish production readiness, maintenance capacity, complete API behavior, or Windows/macOS reliability.

GitHub metadata checked on 2026-10-19 (America/Toronto) returned 1 star for container-zig, created 2026-07-06 with a last push on 2026-07-14. It is about three months old at the time of this report. Its 1.0.0 package version is an upstream version label, not independent evidence of maturity. Source: repository metadata and pinned SDK source.

CandidateWhy it was consideredSelection limitation
container-zigExplicit Zig 0.17 branch, typed Engine operations, version negotiation and local socket support.Very little adoption evidence; one helper compatibility adaptation was required. Chosen to make this experiment possible, not as a production recommendation.
nektro/zig-dockerAn older Docker Engine binding project. GitHub returned 17 stars, creation in 2022 and last push in December 2024.Its published build script uses older APIs such as std.build.Builder and std.builtin.Mode. Code inspection indicates a port is needed for the installed compiler; that alternative was not ported or executed. Repository metadata.
z-ociAnother Zig Docker-related client found during the follow-up search.It targets the OCI/Docker Registry API, not the Docker Engine API used to list local containers.

Stars are an adoption signal, not a code-quality score. The combined evidence here is a short project history, little visible adoption, and a compatibility adjustment already needed in this small integration. The search did not establish a mature current Zig-native Engine SDK; this is not an exhaustive proof that none exists. Go uses the official Moby client; Rust uses the community Bollard client. Treat Zig's row as an experimental integration and assess dependency maturity separately from executable size and idle resource use. Details are retained in sdk-selection.json and the downloadable raw data. The original three integrations and their measurements are preserved. The C SDK and Slint software variants were added and measured separately.

The C SDK variant: real C interop, limited transport

Docker lists danielsuo/libdocker under its unofficial SDKs. It is a small C wrapper over libcurl, with GET/POST and HTTP-status handling, rather than typed container models or automatic API negotiation. GitHub metadata recorded 68 stars, creation in February 2017 and last push in January 2023. An older project and more stars do not establish current maintenance or production readiness.

The pin is 4e6c007615fe151ea59609d5081175ea1fe8e65b. The sole upstream adjustment, retained as libdocker-unix-host.patch, allows a Unix-socket DOCKER_HOST instead of only the hardcoded default socket. Linux is observed; macOS Unix-socket use remains unverified, and Windows named pipes are unsupported by this implementation.

Executable size is not a standalone package size. C libdocker source is compiled into the Zig executable, but libcurl 8.23.0 is a system shared library. The local libcurl file alone is 1.04 MiB, plus its transitive dependencies. Those bytes are outside the executable column. Runtime RSS/PSS include their mapped pages under the normal measurement rules. No complete bundled-distribution size is claimed for any variant; runtime shared-library paths are retained in the C runs' raw data.

Rendering backend matters for this workload

NanoUI’s pinned Linux implementation uses GTK 3 window/input integration, its own CPU rasterizer, and Cairo pixel presentation. Slint also uses CPU rendering here, through its software renderer and Winit window backend. The earlier MyGo runs recorded OpenGL/GLX libraries; GPUI recorded Vulkan/EGL/driver libraries. Loaded libraries identify rendering infrastructure, but do not allocate the measured memory gap to specific components.

The workload is a small list at idle after one API load. It does not demonstrate a GPU advantage for scrolling, live charts, a terminal, high-DPI rendering or animation. GPU rendering can help frequent redraws; CPU rendering can avoid graphics initialization overhead. The figures compare these implementations and configurations, rather than inherent language memory costs. RSS includes resident shared-library pages; PSS apportions shared pages. Compositor/display-server memory and full GPU allocations are outside these process measurements.

Implementation and code ownership

Zig / container-zig

Client.connect negotiates the Docker API; container.list(all=true) returns typed summaries. A worker races the complete load against a standard-library 10-second timer. SDK data is copied into the UI snapshot, then SDK-owned results are released.

The SDK's endpoint-discovery example is imported as a dependency module. One line needed adapting from removed Uri.getHostAlloc to URI-component decoding for the installed Zig 0.17 release. The pinned checkout and container-zig-zig017.patch record the adjustment. No app-specific HTTP or socket protocol was written.

Zig / C libdocker

addTranslateC generates bindings to a small local C bridge. The build compiles the pinned SDK source directly. The bridge calls the SDK's docker_get_with_http_status, configures libcurl lifecycle/timeouts, and copies the response into explicit caller-owned memory. Zig queries /version, selects a supported API version up to 1.55, decodes JSON and maps rows.

The same NanoUI table, search and background-worker structure are retained. A fresh SDK object per request avoids the upstream reused-buffer reset issue. The network requests share a 10-second budget. C adds explicit buffer ownership and linking configuration; this SDK supplies fewer abstractions than the typed Go/Rust/Zig clients. Its small executable is not evidence of equal SDK capability.

Go / official Moby client

client.New(client.FromEnv) handles environment/default configuration and automatic API negotiation. A goroutine calls ContainerList(All:true) under a 10-second context and sends the typed results to the UI thread. The per-refresh client is closed after use.

MyGo still supplies the search field and virtualized table. The SDK replaces the previous file/scanner/subprocess plumbing; the interface is otherwise the same.

Rust / Bollard + gpui-pre

Docker::connect_with_defaults, negotiate_version, and list_containers(all=true) run on a GPUI background worker with a temporary current-thread Tokio runtime. A 10-second Tokio timeout encloses connection, negotiation and listing. The UI receives mapped rows after completion.

The direct GPUI app still owns its text-input widget: 338 code lines in search.rs, plus 264 in main.rs. The GPUI comparison uses gpui-pre; GPUI Kit remains in the original report. Slint is the additional Rust software-rendering variant below.

Rust / Slint software + Bollard

Slint 1.18.1 supplies LineEdit, Button and StandardTableView. Inline Slint UI definitions count alongside Rust in main.rs. There is no local text-editing widget. Docker I/O runs on a worker thread with the same Bollard connect/negotiate/list operations and 10-second Tokio timeout; completion returns through Slint’s event loop. Filtering retains models for matching rows, and the built-in table virtualizes rows.

Only Winit and Slint’s built-in software renderer are enabled. Skia, FemtoVG and WGPU renderers are excluded; the app explicitly selects software rendering. Both Linux window-system features are compiled; the observed window uses X11/XWayland at scale 1. Windows/macOS are supported upstream but unexecuted here. Bollard is pinned identically; the lockfiles resolve Tokio 1.54.0 here versus 1.53.3 in the earlier GPUI variant, so this is not an identical full dependency graph.

Common behavior and limits

All read all container states, disable overlapping Refresh requests, show errors, and retain the last good rows after a failed refresh. More than 20,000 returned rows is an error. Each client buffers/decodes its finite response before that retention check; this is not a common wire-response byte cap.

App line counts include mapping, timeout wiring, proof logging and local input code, excluding blank lines and whole-line comments. The C variant includes its local C bridge and header. Libraries, generated C bindings, upstream endpoint helper, lockfiles, build files and scripts are excluded. These are implementation counts, not a controlled measure of language verbosity.

Refresh observation boundary

The initial live load and its complete container-ID set were observed for all five variants. Refresh is wired to the same SDK loading function in each application. Earlier desktop click automation did not confirm a second load in the original three apps; input delivery versus widget behavior remains unresolved. The C variant’s Refresh button was not separately exercised. Slint startup and its native window were observed, but its scripted search/clear/Refresh inputs also produced no observable change or second load. Slint search and Refresh interactions remain unverified; details are in the raw data. The button interaction is therefore unverified, rather than counted as a pass.

The unsuccessful interaction observations and their logs are retained in refresh-observation.json and embedded in the raw data. They were outside resource measurements. No unit/integration test suite was added or run.

Protocol and portability

Linux measurement protocol

  1. Pin the current context's local Docker endpoint in each child environment using DOCKER_HOST; remove CONTAINER_SNAPSHOT.
  2. Preserve the original three rounds, Zig → Go → Rust. Add C SDK and Slint later, each in three consecutive runs using the same settings. Run one app at a time, after its build is complete. These are not contemporaneously interleaved five-way rounds.
  3. Normalize the client to 1,000 ×680 pixels on X11/XWayland, with GPUI scale1; Slint scale1. Keep the window active and the pointer outside it.
  4. Allow four seconds to settle, then sample process/descendant RSS, PSS and CPU every500ms over twenty seconds.
  5. Read load proof from the app log, compare the complete ID set, capture after the interval, and close only the owned process group.

Observed host: Intel(R) Core(TM) Ultra 7 155H, 22 logical CPUs; Plasma Wayland/XWayland.

What remains platform-dependent

Only the local Linux Unix socket and XWayland windows were observed. Moby and Bollard use DOCKER_HOST/default transports rather than Docker CLI context discovery. The Zig-native variant uses its SDK's endpoint resolver. The C variant only accepts Unix sockets via its small DOCKER_HOST patch and does not support Windows named pipes. Docker Desktop on Mac may need an explicit per-user Unix socket; Windows uses a named pipe.

Bollard is built with its default HTTP/Unix/Windows-pipe client features, without TLS/SSH. Moby's environment configuration and container-zig's transport options have different coverage. Container-zig's SSH transport uses a remote Docker CLI; it was not exercised here. Local direct-socket access is the common measured scope.

Binary sizes exclude system libraries, drivers, debug symbols, and installers. RSS/PSS do not fully describe GPU allocations. No Windows/macOS runtime, large inventory, active interaction performance, continuous update cost, or accessibility result is claimed.
